{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SLuEHPJKXoi6KrxcGuDQBs","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t[![build-openlane-sky130](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master&event=push)](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n2\t\n3\taes\n4\t===\n5\t\n6\tVerilog implementation of the [symmetric block cipher AES (NIST FIPS 197)](http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/fips/fips197/fips-197.pdf).\n7\t\n8\t\n9\t## Status ##\n10\tThe core is completed, has been used in several FPGA and ASIC\n11\tdesigns. The core is well tested and mature.\n12\t\n13\t\n14\t## Introduction ##\n15\t\n16\tThis implementation supports 128 and 256 bit keys. The\n17\timplementation is iterative and process one 128 block at a time. Blocks\n18\tare processed on a word level with 4 S-boxes in the data path. The\n19\tS-boxes for encryption are shared with the key expansion and the core\n20\tcan thus not do key update in parallel with block processing.\n21\t\n22\tThe encipher and decipher block processing datapaths are separated and\n23\tbasically self contained given access to a set of round keys and a\n24\tblock. This makes it possible to hard wire the core to only encipher or\n25\tdecipher operation. This allows the synthesis/build tools to optimize\n26\taway the other functionality which will reduce the size to about\n27\t50%. This has been tested to verify that decryption is removed and the\n28\tcore still works.\n29\t\n30\tFor cipher modes such as CTR, CCM, CMAC, GCM the decryption\n31\tfunctionality in the AES core will never be used and thus the decipher\n32\tblock processing can be removed.\n33\t\n34\tThis is a fairly compact implementation. Further reduction could be\n35\tachived by just having a single S-box. Similarly the performane can be\n36\tincreased by having 8 or even 16 S-boxes which would reduce the number\n37\tof cycles to two cycles for each round.\n38\t\n39\t\n40\t### Contact information ##\n41\t\n42\tAssured provides customer support including customization, integration\n43\tand system development related to the core. The branches are not planned to be merged into master. The\n52\tbranches available that provides versions of the core are:\n53\t\n54\t\n55\t### on-the-fly-keygen ###\n56\t\n57\tThis version of AES implements the key expansion using an on-the-fly\n58\tmechanism. This allows the initial key expansion to be removed. This\n59\tsaves a number of cycles and also remove almost 1800 registers needed to\n60\tstore the round keys. Note that this version of AES only supports\n61\tencryption. On-the-fly key generation does not work with\n62\tdecryption. Decryption must be handled by the block cipher mode - for\n63\texample CTR.\n64\t\n65\t\n66\t### dual-keys ###\n67\t\n68\tThis version of AES supports two separate banks of expanded keys to\n69\tallow fast key switching between two keys. This is useful for example in\n70\tan AEAD mode with CBC + CMAC implemented using a single AES core.\n71\t\n72\t\n73\t### cmt-sbox ###\n74\t\n75\tAn experimental version of the core in which the S-box is implemented\n76\tusing circuit minimized logic functions of a ROM table. The specific\n77\ttable used is\n78\t[the 113 gate circuit](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/SLP_AES_113.txt) by the [CMT team at Yale](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/CMT.html).\n79\t\n80\tSome area and performance results using the cmt_sbox compared to\n81\tmaster:\n82\t\n83\t#### Altera\n84\t- Tool: Quartus Prime 19.1.0\n85\t- Device: Cyclone V (5CGXFC7C7F23C8)\n86\t- master (S-box implemented with a table)\n87\t  - ALMs: 2599\n88\t  - Regs: 3184\n89\t  - Fmax: 93 MHz\n90\t  - aes_sbox: 160 ALUTs\n91\t\n92\t- cmt_sbox\n93\t  - ALMs: 2759\n94\t  - Regs: 3147\n95\t  - Fmax: 69 MHz\n96\t  - aes_sbox: 363 ALUTs\n97\t\n98\t\n99\t#### Xilinx\n100\t- Tool: Vivado 2019.2\n101\t- Device: Kintex-7 (7k70tfbv676-1)\n102\t- master:\n103\t  - LUTs: 3020\n104\t  - FFs: 2992\n105\t  - Fmax: 125 MHz\n106\t\n107\t- cmt_sbox:\n108\t  - LUTs: 2955\n109\t  - FFs: 2992\n110\t  - Fmax: 105 MHz\n111\t\n112\t\n113\t## Core Usage\n114\t\n115\t### Usage sequence:\n116\t1. Load the key to be used by writing to the key register words.\n117\t2. Set the key length by writing to the config register.\n118\t3. Initialize key expansion by writing a one to the init bit in the control register.\n119\t4. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the key expansion has been completed.\n120\t5. Write the cleartext block to the block registers.\n121\t6. Start block processing by writing a one to the next bit in the control register.\n122\t7. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the data block has been processed.\n123\t8. Read out the ciphertext block from the result registers.\n124\t\n125\t\n126\t## FuseSoC\n127\tThis core is supported by the\n128\t[FuseSoC](https://github.com/olofk/fusesoc) core package manager and\n129\tbuild system. #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n514\t    # addroundkey()\n515\t    #\n516\t    # AES AddRoundKey block operation.\n517\t    # Perform XOR combination of the given gm14()\n    #\n    # The specific Galois Multiplication by 14 for a given byte.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def gm14(self, b):\n        return self.gm8(b) ^ self.gm4(b) ^ self.gm2(b)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # substw()\n    #\n    # Returns a 32-bit word in which each of the bytes in the\n    # given 32-bit word has been used as lookup into the AES S-box.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def substw(self, w):\n        (b0, b1, b2, b3) = self.w2b(w)\n        s0 = self.sbox[b0]\n        s1 = self.sbox[b1]\n        s2 = self.sbox[b2]\n        s3 = self.sbox[b3]\n        res = self.b2w(s0, s1, s2, s3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Inside substw:\")\n            print(\"b0 = 0x%02x, b1 = 0x%02x, b2 = 0x%02x, b3 = 0x%02x\" %\n                  (b0, b1, b2, b3))\n            print(\"s0 = 0x%02x, s1 = 0x%02x, s2 = 0x%02x, s3 = 0x%02x\" %\n                  (s0, s1, s2, s3))\n            print(\"res = 0x%08x\" % (res))\n        return res\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # inv_substw()\n    #\n    # Returns a 32-bit word in which each of the bytes in the\n    # given 32-bit word has been used as lookup into\n    # the inverse AES S-box.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def inv_substw(self, w):\n        (b0, b1, b2, b3) = self.w2b(w)\n        s0 = self.inv_sbox[b0]\n        s1 = self.inv_sbox[b1]\n        s2 = self.inv_sbox[b2]\n        s3 = self.inv_sbox[b3]\n        res = self.b2w(s0, s1, s2, s3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Inside inv_substw:\")\n            print(\"b0 = 0x%02x, b1 = 0x%02x, b2 = 0x%02x, b3 = 0x%02x\" %\n                (b0, b1, b2, b3))\n            print(\"s0 = 0x%02x, s1 = 0x%02x, s2 = 0x%02x, s3 = 0x%02x\" %\n                (s0, s1, s2, s3))\n            print(\"res = 0x%08x\" % (res))\n        return res\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # rolx()\n    #\n    # Rotate the given 32 bit word x bits left.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def rolx(self, w, x):\n        return ((w << x) | (w >> (32 - x))) & 0xffffffff\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # next_128bit_key()\n    #\n    # Generate the next four key words for aes-128 based on given\n    # rcon and previous key words.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def next_128bit_key(self, prev_key, rcon):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = prev_key\n\n        rol = self.rolx(w3, 8)\n        subst = self.substw(rol)\n        t = subst ^ (rcon << 24)\n\n        k0 = w0 ^ t\n        k1 = w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n        k2 = w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n        k3 = w3 ^ w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Inside next 128bit key:\")\n            print(\"w0 = 0x%08x, w1 = 0x%08x, w2 = 0x%08x, w3 = 0x%08x\" %\n                  (w0, w1, w2, w3))\n            print(\"rol = 0x%08x, subst = 0x%08x, rcon = 0x%02x, t = 0x%08x\" %\n                  (rol, subst, rcon, t))\n            print(\"k0 = 0x%08x, k1 = 0x%08x, k2 = 0x%08x, k3 = 0x%08x\" %\n                  (k0, k1, k2, k3))\n        return (k0, k1, k2, k3)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # key_gen128()\n    #\n    # Generating the keys for 128 bit keys.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def key_gen128(self, key):\n        print(\"Doing the 128 bit key expansion\")\n\n        round_keys = []\n        round_keys.append(key)\n\n        for i in range(10):\n            round_keys.append(self.next_128bit_key(round_keys[i], self.get_rcon(i + 1)))\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Input key:\")\n            self.print_block(key)\n            print(\"\")\n\n            print(\"Generated keys:\")\n            for k in round_keys:\n                self.print_block(k)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return round_keys\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # next_256bit_key_a()\n    #\n    # Generate the next four key words for aes-256 using algorithm A\n    # based on given rcon and the previous two keys.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def next_256it_key_a(self, key0, key1, rcon):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = key0\n        (w4, w5, w6, w7) = key1\n\n        sw = self.substw(self.rolx(w7, 8))\n        rw = (rcon << 24)\n        t = sw ^ rw\n\n        k0 = w0 ^ t\n        k1 = w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n        k2 = w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n        k3 = w3 ^ w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n\n        if (self.DUMP_VARS):\n            print(\"next_256bit_key_a:\")\n            print(\"w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x\" % (w0, w1, w2, w3))\n            print(\"w4 = 0x%08x, w5 = 0x%08x, w6 = 0x%08x, w7 = 0x%08x\" % (w4, w5, w6, w7))\n            print(\"t = 0x%08x, sw = 0x%08x, rw = 0x%08x\" % (t, sw, rw))\n            print(\"k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x\" % (k0, k1, k2, k3))\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return (k0, k1, k2, k3)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # next_256bit_key_b()\n    #\n    # Generate the next four key words for aes-256 using algorithm B\n    # based on given previous eight keywords.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def next_256it_key_b(self, key0, key1):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = key0\n        (w4, w5, w6, w7) = key1\n\n        t = self.substw(w7)\n\n        k0 = w0 ^ t\n        k1 = w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n        k2 = w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n        k3 = w3 ^ w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t\n\n        if (self.DUMP_VARS):\n            print(\"next_256bit_key_b:\")\n            print(\"w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x\" % (w0, w1, w2, w3))\n            print(\"w4 = 0x%08x, w5 = 0x%08x, w6 = 0x%08x, w7 = 0x%08x\" % (w4, w5, w6, w7))\n            print(\"t = 0x%08x\" % (t))\n            print(\"k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x\" % (k0, k1, k2, k3))\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return (k0, k1, k2, k3)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # key_gen256()\n    #\n    # Generating the keys for 256 bit keys.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def key_gen256(self, key):\n        round_keys = []\n        (k0, k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, k7) = key\n\n        round_keys.append((k0, k1, k2, k3))\n        round_keys.append((k4, k5, k6, k7))\n\n        j = 1\n        for i in range(0, (self.AES_256_ROUNDS - 2), 2):\n            k = self.next_256it_key_a(round_keys[i], round_keys[i + 1], self.get_rcon(j))\n            round_keys.append(k)\n            k = self.next_256it_key_b(round_keys[i + 1], round_keys[i + 2])\n            round_keys.append(k)\n            j += 1\n\n        # One final key needs to be generated.\n        k = self.next_256it_key_a(round_keys[12], round_keys[13], self.get_rcon(7))\n        round_keys.append(k)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Input key:\")\n            self.print_block((k0, k1, k2, k3))\n            self.print_block((k4, k5, k6, k7))\n            print(\"\")\n\n            print(\"Generated keys:\")\n            for k in round_keys:\n                self.print_block(k)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return round_keys\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # get_rcon()\n    #\n    # Function implementation of rcon. Calculates rcon for a\n    # given round. This could be implemented as an iterator.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def get_rcon(self, round):\n        rcon = 0x8d\n\n        for i in range(0, round):\n            rcon = ((rcon << 1) ^ (0x11b & - (rcon >> 7))) & 0xff\n\n        return rcon\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # addroundkey()\n    #\n    # AES AddRoundKey block operation.\n    # Perform XOR combination of the given block and the given key.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def addroundkey(self, key, block):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = block\n        (k0, k1, k2, k3) = key\n\n        res_block = (w0 ^ k0, w1 ^ k1, w2 ^ k2, w3 ^ k3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"AddRoundKey key, block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(key)\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # mixw()\n    #\n    # Perform bit mixing of the given words.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def mixw(self, w):\n        (b0, b1, b2, b3) = self.w2b(w)\n\n        mb0 = self.gm2(b0) ^ self.gm3(b1) ^ b2           ^ b3\n        mb1 = b0           ^ self.gm2(b1) ^ self.gm3(b2) ^ b3\n        mb2 = b0           ^ b1           ^ self.gm2(b2) ^ self.gm3(b3)\n        mb3 = self.gm3(b0) ^ b1           ^ b2           ^ self.gm2(b3)\n\n        return self.b2w(mb0, mb1, mb2, mb3)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # mixcolumns()\n    #\n    # AES MixColumns on the given block.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def mixcolumns(self, block):\n        (c0, c1, c2, c3) = block\n\n        mc0 = self.mixw(c0)\n        mc1 = self.mixw(c1)\n        mc2 = self.mixw(c2)\n        mc3 = self.mixw(c3)\n\n        res_block = (mc0, mc1, mc2, mc3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"MixColumns block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # subbytes()\n    #\n    # AES SubBytes operation on the given block.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def subbytes(self, block):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = block\n\n        res_block = (self.substw(w0), self.substw(w1),\n                    self.substw(w2), self.substw(w3))\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"SubBytes block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # shiftrows()\n    #\n    # AES ShiftRows block operation.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def shiftrows(self, block):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = block\n\n        c0 = self.w2b(w0)\n        c1 = self.w2b(w1)\n        c2 = self.w2b(w2)\n        c3 = self.w2b(w3)\n\n        ws0 = self.b2w(c0[0], c1[1],  c2[2],  c3[3])\n        ws1 = self.b2w(c1[0], c2[1],  c3[2],  c0[3])\n        ws2 = self.b2w(c2[0], c3[1],  c0[2],  c1[3])\n        ws3 = self.b2w(c3[0], c0[1],  c1[2],  c2[3])\n\n        res_block = (ws0, ws1, ws2, ws3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"ShiftRows block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # aes_encipher()\n    #\n    # Perform AES encipher operation for the given block using the\n    # given key length.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def aes_encipher_block(self, key, block):\n        tmp_block = block[:]\n\n        # Get round keys based on the given key.\n        if len(key) == 4:\n            round_keys = self.key_gen128(key)\n            num_rounds = self.AES_128_ROUNDS\n        else:\n            round_keys = self.key_gen256(key)\n            num_rounds = self.AES_256_ROUNDS\n\n        # Init round\n        print(\"  Initial AddRoundKeys round.\")\n        tmp_block4 = self.addroundkey(round_keys[0], block)\n\n        # Main rounds\n        for i in range(1 , (num_rounds)):\n            print(\"\")\n            print(\"  Round %02d\" % i)\n            print(\"  ---------\")\n\n            tmp_block1 = self.subbytes(tmp_block4)\n            tmp_block2 = self.shiftrows(tmp_block1)\n            tmp_block3 = self.mixcolumns(tmp_block2)\n            tmp_block4 = self.addroundkey(round_keys[i], tmp_block3)\n\n\n        # Final round\n        print(\"  Final round.\")\n        tmp_block1 = self.subbytes(tmp_block4)\n        tmp_block2 = self.shiftrows(tmp_block1)\n        tmp_block3 = self.addroundkey(round_keys[num_rounds], tmp_block2)\n\n        return tmp_block3\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # inv_mixw()\n    #\n    # Perform inverse bit mixing of the given words.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def inv_mixw(self, w):\n        (b0, b1, b2, b3) = self.w2b(w)\n\n        mb0 = self.gm14(b0) ^ self.gm11(b1) ^ self.gm13(b2) ^ self.gm09(b3)\n        mb1 = self.gm09(b0) ^ self.gm14(b1) ^ self.gm11(b2) ^ self.gm13(b3)\n        mb2 = self.gm13(b0) ^ self.gm09(b1) ^ self.gm14(b2) ^ self.gm11(b3)\n        mb3 = self.gm11(b0) ^ self.gm13(b1) ^ self.gm09(b2) ^ self.gm14(b3)\n\n        return self.b2w(mb0, mb1, mb2, mb3)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # inv_mixcolumns()\n    #\n    # AES Inverse MixColumns on the given block.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def inv_mixcolumns(self, block):\n        (c0, c1, c2, c3) = block\n\n        mc0 = self.inv_mixw(c0)\n        mc1 = self.inv_mixw(c1)\n        mc2 = self.inv_mixw(c2)\n        mc3 = self.inv_mixw(c3)\n\n        res_block = (mc0, mc1, mc2, mc3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Inverse MixColumns block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # inv_shiftrows()\n    #\n    # AES inverse ShiftRows block operation.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def inv_shiftrows(self, block):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = block\n\n        c0 = self.w2b(w0)\n        c1 = self.w2b(w1)\n        c2 = self.w2b(w2)\n        c3 = self.w2b(w3)\n\n        ws0 = self.b2w(c0[0], c3[1],  c2[2],  c1[3])\n        ws1 = self.b2w(c1[0], c0[1],  c3[2],  c2[3])\n        ws2 = self.b2w(c2[0], c1[1],  c0[2],  c3[3])\n        ws3 = self.b2w(c3[0], c2[1],  c1[2],  c0[3])\n\n        res_block = (ws0, ws1, ws2, ws3)\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Inverse ShiftRows block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # inv_subbytes()\n    #\n    # AES inverse SubBytes operation on the given block.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def inv_subbytes(self, block):\n        (w0, w1, w2, w3) = block\n\n        res_block = (self.inv_substw(w0), self.inv_substw(w1),\n                     self.inv_substw(w2), self.inv_substw(w3))\n\n        if (self.VERBOSE):\n            print(\"Inverse SubBytes block in and block out:\")\n            self.print_block(block)\n            self.print_block(res_block)\n            print(\"\")\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # aes_decipher()\n    #\n    # Perform AES decipher operation for the given block\n    # using the given key length.\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def aes_decipher_block(self, key, block):\n        tmp_block = block[:]\n\n        # Get round keys based on the given key.\n        if len(key) == 4:\n            round_keys = self.key_gen128(key)\n            num_rounds = self.AES_128_ROUNDS\n        else:\n            round_keys = self.key_gen256(key)\n            num_rounds = self.AES_256_ROUNDS\n\n            # Initial round\n        print(\"  Initial, partial round.\")\n        tmp_block1 = self.addroundkey(round_keys[len(round_keys) - 1], tmp_block)\n        tmp_block2 = self.inv_shiftrows(tmp_block1)\n        tmp_block4 = self.inv_subbytes(tmp_block2)\n\n        # Main rounds\n        for i in range(1 , (num_rounds)):\n            print(\"\")\n            print(\"  Round %02d\" % i)\n            print(\"  ---------\")\n\n            tmp_block1 = self.addroundkey(round_keys[(len(round_keys) - i - 1)], tmp_block4)\n            tmp_block2 = self.inv_mixcolumns(tmp_block1)\n            tmp_block3 = self.inv_shiftrows(tmp_block2)\n            tmp_block4 = self.inv_subbytes(tmp_block3)\n\n        # Final round\n        print(\"  Final AddRoundKeys round.\")\n        res_block = self.addroundkey(round_keys[0], tmp_block4)\n\n        return res_block\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # test_mixcolumns()\n    #\n    # Test the print(\"invmixword: 0x%08x\" % inv_mixresult)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # single_aes_test()\n    #\n    # Perform a single AES operation and check result\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    def single_aes_test(self, title, encdec, key, block, expected):\n        print(title)\n        self.print_key(key)\n        self.print_block(block)\n\n        if encdec == \"encipher\":\n            result = self.aes_encipher_block(key, block)\n        else:\n            result = self.aes_decipher_block(key, block)\n        return self.check_block(result, expected)\n\n\n    #-------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # test_aes()\n    #\n    # {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NWynF3DfFhSduLK1g3qagX","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t[![build-openlane-sky130](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master&event=push)](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n2\t\n3\taes\n4\t===\n5\t\n6\tVerilog implementation of the [symmetric block cipher AES (NIST FIPS 197)](http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/fips/fips197/fips-197.pdf).\n7\t\n8\t\n9\t## Status ##\n10\tThe core is completed, has been used in several FPGA and ASIC\n11\tdesigns. The core is well tested and mature.\n12\t\n13\t\n14\t## Introduction ##\n15\t\n16\tThis implementation supports 128 and 256 bit keys. The\n17\timplementation is iterative and process one 128 block at a time. Blocks\n18\tare processed on a word level with 4 S-boxes in the data path. The\n19\tS-boxes for encryption are shared with the key expansion and the core\n20\tcan thus not do key update in parallel with block processing.\n21\t\n22\tThe encipher and decipher block processing datapaths are separated and\n23\tbasically self contained given access to a set of round keys and a\n24\tblock. This makes it possible to hard wire the core to only encipher or\n25\tdecipher operation. This allows the synthesis/build tools to optimize\n26\taway the other functionality which will reduce the size to about\n27\t50%. This has been tested to verify that decryption is removed and the\n28\tcore still works.\n29\t\n30\tFor cipher modes such as CTR, CCM, CMAC, GCM the decryption\n31\tfunctionality in the AES core will never be used and thus the decipher\n32\tblock processing can be removed.\n33\t\n34\tThis is a fairly compact implementation. Further reduction could be\n35\tachived by just having a single S-box. Similarly the performane can be\n36\tincreased by having 8 or even 16 S-boxes which would reduce the number\n37\tof cycles to two cycles for each round.\n38\t\n39\t\n40\t### Contact information ##\n41\t\n42\tAssured provides customer support including customization, integration\n43\tand system development related to the core. For more information,\n44\tplease contact [Assured Security\n45\tConsultants](https://www.assured.se/contact).\n46\t\n47\t\n48\t## Branches ##\n49\t\n50\tThere are several branches available that provides different versions of\n51\tthe core. The branches are not planned to be merged into master. The\n52\tbranches available that provides versions of the core are:\n53\t\n54\t\n55\t### on-the-fly-keygen ###\n56\t\n57\tThis version of AES implements the key expansion using an on-the-fly\n58\tmechanism. This allows the initial key expansion to be removed. This\n59\tsaves a number of cycles and also remove almost 1800 registers needed to\n60\tstore the round keys. Note that this version of AES only supports\n61\tencryption. On-the-fly key generation does not work with\n62\tdecryption. Decryption must be handled by the block cipher mode - for\n63\texample CTR.\n64\t\n65\t\n66\t### dual-keys ###\n67\t\n68\tThis version of AES supports two separate banks of expanded keys to\n69\tallow fast key switching between two keys. The core is well tested and mature.\n\n\n## Introduction ##\n\nThis implementation supports 128 and 256 bit keys. The\nimplementation is iterative and process one 128 block at a time. Blocks\nare processed on a word level with 4 S-boxes in the data path. The\nS-boxes for encryption are shared with the key expansion and the core\ncan thus not do key update in parallel with block processing.\n\nThe encipher and decipher block processing datapaths are separated and\nbasically self contained given access to a set of round keys and a\nblock. This makes it possible to hard wire the core to only encipher or\ndecipher operation. This allows the synthesis/build tools to optimize\naway the other functionality which will reduce the size to about\n50%. This has been tested to verify that decryption is removed and the\ncore still works.\n\nFor cipher modes such as CTR, CCM, CMAC, GCM the decryption\nfunctionality in the AES core will never be used and thus the decipher\nblock processing can be removed.\n\nThis is a fairly compact implementation. Further reduction could be\nachived by just having a single S-box. Similarly the performane can be\nincreased by having 8 or even 16 S-boxes which would reduce the number\nof cycles to two cycles for each round.\n\n\n### Contact information ##\n\nAssured provides customer support including customization, integration\nand system development related to the core. For more information,\nplease contact [Assured Security\nConsultants](https://www.assured.se/contact).\n\n\n## Branches ##\n\nThere are several branches available that provides different versions of\nthe core. The branches are not planned to be merged into master. The\nbranches available that provides versions of the core are:\n\n\n### on-the-fly-keygen ###\n\nThis version of AES implements the key expansion using an on-the-fly\nmechanism. This allows the initial key expansion to be removed. This\nsaves a number of cycles and also remove almost 1800 registers needed to\nstore the round keys. Note that this version of AES only supports\nencryption. On-the-fly key generation does not work with\ndecryption. Decryption must be handled by the block cipher mode - for\nexample CTR.\n\n\n### dual-keys ###\n\nThis version of AES supports two separate banks of expanded keys to\nallow fast key switching between two keys. This is useful for example in\nan AEAD mode with CBC + CMAC implemented using a single AES core.\n\n\n### cmt-sbox ###\n\nAn experimental version of the core in which the S-box is implemented\nusing circuit minimized logic functions of a ROM table. The specific\ntable used is\n[the 113 gate circuit](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/SLP_AES_113.txt) by the [CMT team at Yale](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/CMT.html).\n\nSome area and performance results using the cmt_sbox compared to\nmaster:\n\n#### Altera\n- Tool: Quartus Prime 19.1.0\n- Device: Cyclone V (5CGXFC7C7F23C8)\n- master (S-box implemented with a table)\n  - ALMs: 2599\n  - Regs: 3184\n  - Fmax: 93 MHz\n  - aes_sbox: 160 ALUTs\n\n- cmt_sbox\n  - ALMs: 2759\n  - Regs: 3147\n  - Fmax: 69 MHz\n  - aes_sbox: 363 ALUTs\n\n\n#### Xilinx\n- Tool: Vivado 2019.2\n- Device: Kintex-7 (7k70tfbv676-1)\n- master:\n  - LUTs: 3020\n  - FFs: 2992\n  - Fmax: 125 MHz\n\n- cmt_sbox:\n  - LUTs: 2955\n  - FFs: 2992\n  - Fmax: 105 MHz\n\n\n## Core Usage\n\n### Usage sequence:\n1. Load the key to be used by writing to the key register words.\n2. Set the key length by writing to the config register.\n3. Initialize key expansion by writing a one to the init bit in the control register.\n4. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the key expansion has been completed.\n5. Write the cleartext block to the block registers.\n6. Start block processing by writing a one to the next bit in the control register.\n7. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the data block has been processed.\n8. Read out the ciphertext block from the result registers.\n\n\n## FuseSoC\nThis core is supported by the\n[FuseSoC](https://github.com/olofk/fusesoc) core package manager and\nbuild system. Some quick  FuseSoC instructions:\n\ninstall FuseSoC\n~~~\npip install fusesoc\n~~~\n\nCreate and enter a new workspace\n~~~\nmkdir workspace && cd workspace\n~~~\n\nRegister aes as a library in the workspace\n~~~\nfusesoc library add aes /path/to/aes\n~~~\n\n...if repo is available locally or...\n...to get the upstream repo\n~~~\nfusesoc library add aes https://github.com/secworks/aes\n~~~\n\nTo run lint\n~~~\nfusesoc run --target=lint secworks:crypto:aes\n~~~\n\nRun tb_aes testbench\n~~~\nfusesoc run --target=tb_aes secworks:crypto:aes\n~~~\n\nRun with modelsim instead of default tool (icarus)\n~~~\nfusesoc run --target=tb_aes --tool=modelsim secworks:crypto:aes\n~~~\n\nList all targets\n~~~\nfusesoc core show secworks:crypto:aes\n~~~\n\n\n## Implementation results - ASIC ##\n\nThe core has been implemented in standard cell ASIC processes.\n\n### TSMC 180 nm ###\nTarget frequency: 20 MHz\nComplete flow from RTL to placed gates. Automatic clock gating and scan\ninsertion.\n\n- 8 kCells\n- Aera: 520 x 520 um\n- Good timing margin with no big cells and buffers.\n\n\n## Implementation results - FPGA ##\n\nThe core has been implemented in Altera and Xilinx FPGA devices.\n\n### Altera Cyclone V GX ###\n- 2624 ALMs\n- 3123 Regs\n- 96 MHz\n- 46 cycles/block\n\n\n### Altera Cyclone IV GX ###\n- 7426 LEs\n- 2994 Regs\n- 96 MHz fmax\n- 46 cycles/block\n\nThis means that we can do more than 2 Mblocks/s or 256 Mbps\nperformance.\n\nRemoving the decipher module yields:\n- 5497 LEs\n- 2855 Regs\n- 106 MHz fmax\n- 46 cycles/block\n\n\n### Microchip IGLOO 2 ###\n- Tool: Libero v 12.4\n- Device: M2GL090TS-1FG484I\n- LUTs: 6335\n- SLEs: 1376\n- BRAMs: 8\n- Fmax: 98.5 MHz\n\n\n### Xilinx Spartan6LX-3 ###\n- 2576 slices\n- 3000 regs\n- 100 MHz\n- 46 cycles/block\n\n\n### Xilinx Artix 7 200T-3 ###\n- 2298 slices\n- 2989 regs\n- 97 MHz\n- 46 cycles/block\n","numLines":235,"startLine":1,"totalLines":235}}}
